fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. Semantic scores in this file must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.
summary: Two material changes since the prior snapshot: Taiwan's central bank kept its policy rate at 2.0%, raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 11.48%, and modestly eased second-home credit restrictions; meanwhile preliminary ship tracking showed only three commercial vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, materially worsening evidence of physical shipping impairment. Saudi alternative loading via Oman has eased crude-price pressure, but Hormuz/Red Sea and refined-product risks remain very high.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: Taiwan's rate hold avoids an immediate domestic discount-rate shock and the central bank's 11.48% 2026 growth forecast confirms exceptional AI/export-led momentum. Selective housing-credit easing is incrementally supportive for banks, property and domestic demand. However, Fed tightening, dollar strength and severe Hormuz/Red Sea disruption keep imported-energy, FX and global valuation risks elevated.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market observations and semantic scores are research evidence only.

key_drivers.name: Taiwan central bank holds at 2% and upgrades growth
key_drivers.observed: The CBC kept the discount rate at 2.0%, raised its 2026 GDP forecast to 11.48% and forecasts 5.82% growth in 2027. It forecasts 2026 headline/core CPI at 2.03%/2.16% and 2027 at 1.83%/1.89%. From September 18 the maximum LTV for a natural person's second home rises from 60% to 70%, without a grace period.
key_drivers.interpretation: No immediate domestic rate shock despite the Fed hike; strong AI/export momentum is officially acknowledged, while selective credit easing marginally supports property-related liquidity.

key_drivers.name: Hormuz observed vessel traffic collapses
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported only three commercial vessels transited Hormuz on Wednesday, down from 12 the prior day and below a 10-day average of 17; AIS-dark traffic can make counts incomplete.
key_drivers.interpretation: Physical shipping impairment has materially worsened even as alternative Saudi crude routing mitigates outright supply loss. Tail risks remain high for LNG, crude, insurance and freight.

key_drivers.name: Saudi alternative routing tempers crude prices
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported Brent near $104.33 and WTI near $101.34 as additional Saudi loadings off Sohar eased immediate supply concerns.
key_drivers.interpretation: Crude availability has a partial workaround, but this does not resolve Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb or refined-product scarcity.

key_risks: Further Fed hikes lift front-end yields, DXY and equity discount rates.
Only three observed commercial Hormuz transits on Wednesday signal severe physical shipping impairment.
Concurrent Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb disruption threatens crude/LNG availability, freight and marine insurance.
Russian refinery outages and export restrictions sustain diesel/jet-fuel scarcity.
Taiwan core CPI forecast remains above 2% for 2026 despite the CBC hold.
VIX, copper, USD/TWD and exact Treasury closes remain stale in this semantic snapshot.

policy_tone.fed: Hawkish tightening: target range 3.75%-4.00%; September projections indicate further tightening risk.
policy_tone.taiwan_central_bank: Hold with selective credit easing: policy rate remains 2.0%; second-home maximum LTV rises to 70% from September 18; growth forecast upgraded strongly.
policy_tone.china: No new monetary-policy action incorporated; August youth unemployment deterioration is a demand/labor-market risk.
policy_tone.global: Energy shock remains inflationary and growth-negative despite partial Saudi crude-routing mitigation.

events.observed_evidence: Preliminary ship-tracking data cited by Reuters showed only three commercial vessels transited Hormuz on Wednesday, down from 12 the prior day and below the recent 10-day average of 17. Bab el-Mandeb crossings were 21 versus 24 the prior day. AIS-dark movements may not be captured.
events.semantic_interpretation: The low observed transit count is stronger evidence of physical chokepoint impairment than price moves alone. Saudi routing via Oman mitigates some crude-export loss but does not remove LNG, insurance, freight or wider regional escalation risk.
